analysis.title: Is The Worst Of The Tech Unwind Over? Goldman's Privorotsky Runs The Checklist As Inflation Swaps Crater
key_insights: Goldman's Privorotsky says Monday 11/9 was a strong recovery: tech back on the front foot, Nvidia weakness compartmentalized, energy sharply lower. He calls the prior drawdown one of the most aggressive episodes of net/gross de-risking in the GS US prime book in a decade.
The drawdown was especially painful because momentum and high beta unwound together, which compounded losses in the most leveraged exposures and drove strong low-volatility outperformance.

The re-grossing trade Privorotsky sees is rate curve steepening, growth expectations recovering and high beta/momentum regaining leadership. The trigger is a bond rally: if CPI gives bonds a reason to rally, short covering could turn into a more sustainable re-grossing cycle.

Oil: Brent fell almost 6% on Monday after Trump cited positive momentum toward ending the Iran war. Privorotsky calls it 'containment, not de-escalation' and sees risk as two-sided after a fast repricing, so he is staying balanced. If flows normalize without further infrastructure damage, the oil risk premium has further to unwind.

Privorotsky thinks the market misread the midterm elections. The likely outcome is data centers built with more conditions attached, not a nationwide moratorium, which favors infrastructure and well-capitalized developers.
The bipartisan permitting bill cleared its first Senate procedural hurdle 73-25 on Monday. Privorotsky cautions that final passage is far off and the House is likely the bigger obstacle.

Constellation Energy (CEG) rose 10% after Q3 adjusted EPS of $5.06 against roughly $3.90 consensus, a second raise of the guidance midpoint this year, and agreements adding more than 1,000 MW of new generation. Privorotsky says this reinforces that the physical buildout continues.

October CPI was due at 8:30am ET on 11/10, with roughly 80% odds of a December Fed hike priced. There is no year-over-year figure because of last year's shutdown, so the market trades core MoM to the second decimal. Goldman economists forecast headline +0.21% MoM vs +0.3% consensus and core +0.16% vs +0.22% consensus. Privorotsky: core at 0.2% would be constructive and 0.3% would challenge the rally.
Treasury supply is heavy: $42B in 10-year notes on 11/10 after a relatively weak 3-year auction, then $25B in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
Privorotsky notes the 10-year barely responded to Brent's near 6% drop, and concludes rates are more reflexive to AI growth expectations than to energy.

The 2-year inflation swap fell from about 2.64% in mid-October to 2.18% (about 45bps in three weeks). That is almost 100bps below the May high of 3.13% and 2bps above the August low. Privorotsky says inflation expectations are rolling over quickly and rate hike expectations may follow.

The NY Fed consumer survey shows household inflation expectations near a 3-year high (about 3.9% per the author), a gap with the 2.2% in swap pricing. The author doubts a Fed that has been hiking will rely on swaps.

Nvidia: the market compartmentalized the news about Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Privorotsky says leadership uncertainty is not the same as deteriorating AI demand, and the broader complex trading independently is a positive signal.

CoreWeave reports 11/10, the first neocloud report since the midterms. Privorotsky's question is whether contracted capacity translates into attractive returns after financing costs, delays and depreciation. His bear case is that the worry is potential compute oversupply or efficiency gains in the medium to long term, not undersupply.

Privorotsky's checklist: energy supportive, rates supportive, credit resilient, positioning and sentiment still shell shocked. If energy and inflation cooperate, the year-end setup looks increasingly attractive. His list: aerospace, transports, select discretionary, high quality/unlevered AI.

His bottom line is broadly encouraged. Much of the initial bounce has happened, which makes aggressive chasing difficult ahead of CPI, but SPX December upside back to 13 vol makes it easier to stay invested. Caveats: a violent rally off the lows, vol that tends to be autocorrelated, and hot CPI or Middle East escalation into the weekend as the main risks.
The article's author (ZeroHedge) expects a squeeze first and a shorter re-grossing cycle than the desk hopes, especially if CoreWeave's numbers show returns after financing costs.
